title: SQL views: interfaces, updates, and access
summary: Create views, trace their results, and explain update and security boundaries.
intro: An ordinary view names a stored query definition. It can become a useful interface, but does not automatically become a stored copy of rows, a performance cache, or a complete security boundary.
outcomes: Create filtered and grouped view definitions.
Predict view results after a visible base-table change.
Distinguish updateability, CHECK OPTION, materialization, and privileges.

sections.title: 1. Define the interface
paragraphs: A view exposes columns and rows selected by a query. Consumers can query its name similarly to a table, but the underlying work still depends on its definition and plan. A grouped course summary has one output row per course, not one per enrolment.

Run CREATE VIEW once after setup. Repeating it without dropping or replacing the existing object is expected to fail. Product-specific CREATE OR REPLACE or CREATE OR ALTER forms are not interchangeable.
sections.code:
CREATE VIEW U3CourseSummary AS
SELECT c.course_code, COUNT(e.student_id) AS enrolled
FROM U3Course c
LEFT JOIN U3Enrolment e ON e.course_code = c.course_code
GROUP BY c.course_code;

SELECT course_code, enrolled
FROM U3CourseSummary
ORDER BY course_code;

sections.title: 2. Trace the definition to its rows
paragraphs: U3CourseSummary starts from Course, preserves AI101 with an outer join, and counts actual child matches. If a new AI101 enrolment is committed and visible to the reader, a subsequent ordinary-view query shows its count as one without a separate refresh.

The returned rows can still reflect transaction snapshots. Another session's uncommitted INSERT is not guaranteed to become visible merely because a view was queried. An ordinary view is not a mechanism for bypassing transaction visibility.
sections.alt: Base course and enrolment tables feed a stored view query definition. Query execution computes three summary rows. A materialized result is shown separately as stored rows requiring refresh.
sections.caption: Store a definition versus store a result. These two designs have different freshness and maintenance obligations.

sections.title: 3. Why a view may not be updateable
paragraphs: A simple view over one table may support unambiguous changes. A grouped count cannot generally be translated into one unique base-table modification: setting enrolled to 7 does not specify which students to insert. Joins, DISTINCT, aggregates, and computed columns introduce product-specific restrictions.

Do not teach that every view is read-only or every view is updateable. Oracle and PostgreSQL have rules for automatically updateable cases and mechanisms such as INSTEAD OF triggers for selected alternatives. A trigger can implement an interface policy, but that policy must still be designed.

sections.title: 4. CHECK OPTION protects the view predicate
paragraphs: For an updateable MCA-only student view, an update that changes programme to MBA would make the row disappear from the view. WITH CHECK OPTION can reject a change made through the view that violates its defining condition. It does not automatically prevent the owner from editing the base table directly.

A view can expose selected columns instead of a private email field. Grant consumers access only through the intended interface and check the DBMS rules for view owner/invoker rights, functions, and underlying access. Hiding a column in a page while still granting unrestricted base-table SELECT is not access control.

sections.title: 5. Materialized results and maintenance trade-offs
paragraphs: A materialized view or other persisted summary stores result rows and needs a refresh strategy. It may reduce repeated expensive work but can be stale and consumes storage. Engines offer different features; do not call an ordinary view materialized because it has an index-friendly query.

Exercise: compare a live grouped view with a separately stored snapshot after inserting one AI101 enrolment. The ordinary view recomputes under its visibility rules; a manually stored snapshot stays unchanged until maintained. Explain the application's acceptable freshness before recommending either design.

revision: Explain the view result at its grain and derive AI101's zero count.
State the conditions for an unambiguous view update.
Distinguish predicate enforcement, access privileges, and cached results.

questions.question: Does CREATE VIEW copy the five enrolments?
answer: An ordinary view stores a query definition, not an independent persisted copy of its result. Execution can still use working memory or temporary storage. A materialized result is a different object or design.

questions.question: Why is changing a grouped count ambiguous?
answer: The requested count does not identify which child rows should be added or removed. Several incompatible base-table changes could produce the same number, so a general automatic translation is unavailable.

questions.question: Is a view that omits email sufficient to keep email private?
answer: Only if the access design prevents bypassing that interface and its execution semantics are appropriate. A user with direct base-table access can still read email. Review privileges and function/view execution rights.
